Storagek8s 1.35

StatefulSet volumeClaimTemplates

Why does every replica of a StatefulSet get its own disk, when Deployment replicas that name a claim all share that one? The volumeClaimTemplate stamps out one PersistentVolumeClaim per ordinal with a deterministic name like data-web-0 rather than a random one. Because that name comes from the Pod identity, a recreated Pod, even on another Node, mounts the same claim and data. Scaling down leaves the claims behind, as the default retention policy is Retain.

▶ Play the animation 5 steps, animated, best on a wide screen

How it works, step by step

  1. One ordinal at a time, the StatefulSet creates the claim and then its Pod. The claim name is not random: it is the template name joined to the Pod name, data-web-0, data-web-1, data-web-2. Under the default OrderedReady policy, web-1 waits until web-0 is Running and Ready.

    Play from this step

  2. Each claim is bound to its own PersistentVolume, so ordinal 0 gets PV web-0 and never touches ordinal 1. Drawn as one phase here, by default each ordinal binds and mounts before the next is created. The claim is the durable name, the disk behind it stores the bytes.

    Play from this step

  3. Each Pod starts and mounts the volume behind its own claim. Replica web-0 reads and writes data-web-0, web-1 data-web-1, and so on. Each replica names a different claim and a claim binds exactly one PV, so no two replicas share a disk.

    Play from this step

  4. Delete web-1 and the StatefulSet recreates it, possibly on another Node that can reach PV web-1. The claim data-web-1 is not deleted with the Pod and stays Bound to PV web-1. The new Pod derives the same claim name from its ordinal, so it mounts the very same disk and data.

    Play from this step

  5. Scale web down to two and Pod web-2 is removed, but claim data-web-2 stays Bound with its data. That is the default retention policy, Retain, which the StatefulSet PVC Retention card covers. Scale back up and web-2 reuses the same claim, but a scale-down nobody cleans up leaves disks behind.

    Play from this step
